meta.title: commit-predict-reveal · constrained decoding
meta.lede: Wrapped around mass-reseat: before the masked odds are counted, the film asks what USD’s share becomes. The guess rides to an axis; the count lands beside it.
meta.synthesis: The wrapper splices two freezes into the inner’s clock — ask + commit before the payoff, a gap bracket after it — and touches nothing else. On the page the clock waits for your guess; in the video the card fills with an illustrative answer and says so.
sources: Outlines · XGrammar — masks precomputed per grammar state

params.question: After the mask, USD’s share of the odds?

params.means: each mark is 1/1,000 of the probability mass

control.label: Constrain
control.question: Mask off: which token does the same draw take?

captions.in.queue: Before each token, the model scores every candidate.
captions.in.close: The schema allows USD, US, EUR or MXN: four tracks close.
captions.in.reseat: Their weight rides back and re-seats on the open tracks.
captions.ask: Before the count: what share of the odds does USD hold now?
captions.commit: Pause and guess. A common intuition: unchanged, 42 %.
captions.gap: The intuition was 26 points low: masking renormalises.
captions.in.hold: Nothing new for a moment: the odds moved, none were lost.
captions.in.name: Mask, then renormalise: each kept p is divided by the kept mass.

meta.title: commit-predict-reveal · the cab problem
meta.lede: Kahneman’s cab problem with a commit before the reveal: the most common answer is 80 %; the count says 41 %.
meta.synthesis: The card is drawn before the words, the countdown is visible, and the guess becomes a mark on the same axis as the counted answer. The gap bracket never shames: most of us land near 80.
sources: Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow, ch. 16 (Causes Trump Statistics)

po.label: A cab hit someone at night. A witness says it was Blue.

params.question: The witness says Blue. What is the chance the cab was Blue?

foot.queue: each dot is one cab · only {groupPct} of the city’s cabs are Blue
foot.close: test her on every cab: 150 × 0.8 = {n:blue-saysBlue} Blue · 850 × 0.2 = {n:green-saysBlue} Green
foot.reseat: the other {droppedN} stay, faint: still in the city, no longer in the question
foot.countOff: no witness: the answer is the base rate, {groupN} of {N}

control.label: Use the witness
control.question: Without the witness, what is the chance the cab was Blue?

notes: the 80 % reliability is the textbook’s, tested at night

captions.in.queue: A city of 1,000 cabs: 150 Blue, 850 Green.
captions.in.close: Test the witness on every cab: 290 would be called Blue.
captions.in.reseat: Only those 290 are still in question.
captions.ask: Before the count: the witness says Blue. What is the chance it was?
captions.commit: Pause and guess. Hold your number.
captions.in.count: Count the Blue ones: 120 of 290. About 41 %.
captions.gap: Most of us land near 80. The count says 41.
captions.in.hold: Most cabs called Blue are Green.
captions.in.name: The base rate decides.
